To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
hair bleaching agents cause damage to hair by increasing the permeability of the hair, and the diffusion of metal ions into the hair.
hair bleaching agents can damage the ultrastructure of hair and that the damage is related to the strength of the bleaching agent.
bleaching agents can penetrate the cortex of hair and decompose melanin granules.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an ideal hair bleaching agent that does not damage hair.
the mechanism of hair damage caused by hair bleaching, which may be useful for the development of new hair bleaching agents.
the development of a bleaching agent which causes the minimum of hair damage.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the bleaching action is the decomposition and diffusion of melanin granular contents, which causes the damage to hair.

the damage to human hair is mainly caused by the decomposition of melanins by bleaching agents, and the decomposition of melanines leads to the flow out of melanine granules and the diffusion of the granular contents into outside of the melanin granule, and the diffusion of metal ions into the melanin granula and intermacrofibrilar matrix.
bleaching agents cause hair damage by two mechanisms: the decomposition of the melanin granule structure and the catalytic action of metal ions with hydrogen peroxide outside the melanin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the bleaching agent with the stronger bleaching effect causes more damage to human hair than the bleaching agent of weak effect, and the damage is mainly caused by the decomposition of melanins and the diffusion of the metal elements into the hair cortex.

the bleaching action provoked decomposition of melanin and flow out of melanin granular contents to intermacrofibril matrix, and the metal elements diffusing into the intermacrofil matrix promoted further damage of hair by catalytic reaction with hydrogen peroxide in bleaching agents outside of melanin granule.
the damage to human hair caused by bleaching agents can be reduced by the use of an appropriate bleaching agent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the bleaching action provoked a decomposition of melanin and a flow out of the granular contents into intermacrofibril matrix, which promoted damage to the hair.
the damage to human hair caused by the bleaching agent can be reduced by controlling the permeability of the hair and by reducing the catalytic activity of metal elements in the bleaching agent.
